producer_report.summary: A "try again on <job>" reader brief now carries the retried job's last reading and the user's corrections. The reading covers its summary, acceptance criteria, deliverables and out-of-scope items. The corrections come from the whole retry chain. The brief says the rejected attempt's changes were discarded and are not in the repository. It also says the original request's scope still applies and the corrections must be kept. A brief with no earlier attempt is unchanged. All three checks pass.

checks_run.note: Run before the final changelog edit; no Rust changed after it.
Every test result line shows 0 failed, including the extended retry lifecycle tests in athena-cli.

open_issues: The brief's Earlier attempt section is not described in any docs page (searched `docs/`), so I made no docs edit. The only documentation change is the CHANGELOG entry.
`run.rs` needed no change: it already passes the `EarlierAttempt` from `earlier_attempt()` through.
I did not run the full test suite again after the changelog edit; no code changed after the last `cargo test`.
mistakes: I ran `grep` through Bash and the hook blocked it. I used the Grep tool after that.
I tried to read the saved `cargo test` output from outside the working directory and was denied. I re-ran `cargo test --locked --quiet` instead.
learnings: `EarlierAttempt` is built only in `carry()`, in `reading.rs`, and `carry()` also feeds `referenced_jobs`. I put the reading and corrections in a separate `carry_reading()`, called only from `earlier_attempt()`. That keeps referenced jobs unchanged.

The `reading()` helper in the `briefs.rs` tests is `pub(crate)`, so `reading.rs` tests cannot build a `Reading` with it. The `reading.rs` unit test covers the chain corrections, redaction and the rendered brief. The lifecycle tests cover the reading text end to end.
